blocks.text: The man outside the grocery did not move aside.
Laura slowed. He had a newspaper folded beneath one arm and a stain down the front of his white coat. His glasses made his eyes look too large.
Behind him, the grocer stood in his doorway. He had been pointing along the street. When he saw Laura, his hand dropped.
The man turned.
“Daniel Orkleson,” the man said. “I've been asking about the woman from the paper.”
Laura stopped a few feet from him. “What do you want?”
“What you can do interests me. With the right equipment—”
“I've already had somebody tell me useful things I could do with it.”
She stepped around him. He let her pass.
“Was that Flaming Head?” Daniel tried the name and watched her face.
Laura stopped. “You know him?”
“We've met. He interfered with my work.”
“Then you know how he likes giving lessons. He did this to me. Now he wants me pleased because I can hit a target.”
Daniel tucked the newspaper more securely beneath his arm. “What did you want?”
She studied him through the mask. He had not stepped back once.
“What are you offering?”
“A chance to work together.”
“Why should I join you?”
“I created a device that will drain the power from that fireball with a face.”
blocks.alt: Daniel approaches masked Laura on the shopping street and offers an alliance while ordinary pedestrians keep their distance.

blocks.text: “You can take his power away?”
“With your help.”
“Have you done it?”
“I've collected energy of this kind before. There are preparations to complete.”

She heard the gap in his answer. She could also picture the little face above the rocks, waiting to give another lesson, and wondered how he would like being unable to float away from what had happened.
“Would draining him change me?”
“Not necessarily. They're different problems.”
She let the edge of her coat fall open again.
“I want to see it.”
Daniel stepped toward the corner.
“This way.”
Luke heard the side door scrape and rose from behind a cabinet.

Daniel had spent the days since the move rebuilding a collector. That afternoon he had gone to find the woman from the newspaper, leaving Luke to search for a ceramic connector. Luke had found one that might fit and left it on the cabinet, saving the news to make his uncle stop and listen.
“Did you—”
The woman stepped through behind his uncle.
Luke stopped above the cabinet.
She was wearing the mask from the newspaper. The flames on her black suit were bright even in the dim workshop.
Daniel pulled the door shut.
“Mind the piece of timber,” he told her. “The catch is unreliable.”
Laura stepped over it. Her eyes traveled across the benches, then to the tank standing beside the loading entrance.
She stopped walking.
“Is that real?”
“Very.”
She moved far enough to see the tracks and the long gun above them. A few days earlier, she had been standing in front of an old baking sheet. Here was something that took up half a room.
Daniel watched her take it in.
“A little more space than I'm accustomed to,” he said. “But we're making use of it.”
blocks.alt: Laura enters the relocated workshop beside Daniel and takes in the full-size tank while bodyless Luke watches her arrival with alarm.

blocks.text: Luke came out from behind the cabinet.
“You brought her here?”
Laura turned toward his voice.
Her gaze moved from his hair to the bolts at the sides of his face, then down to the iron jaw. She looked below it, where there was nothing to see.
“She's going to help us,” Daniel said.
Luke looked at the flame pattern on her suit.
“She's one of them.”
Laura turned back to Daniel.
“What's with this monstrosity?”
Luke went very still.
“I can hear you.”
“Then you heard me.”
blocks.alt: Laura dismissively gestures toward bodyless Luke while addressing Daniel; Luke looks hurt and angry and Daniel impatiently turns toward his work.

blocks.text: Daniel put the newspaper on a bench.
“This is my nephew, Luke.”
He waited just long enough for Laura to look back at him, then waved toward the room beyond the tank.
“The work I mentioned is over here.”
Luke stayed in their way.
“You don't know her,” Luke said. “And you brought her in here?”
Laura folded her arms. The floating head watched her as though she had slipped through a window.
“Where did you get the suit?”
She looked down at herself.
“Flaming Head gave it to me.”
“And we're supposed to believe you're not working together?”
Laura's arms tightened across her coat.
“I'm finished taking instructions from him.”
“A present from him, and now you want to work with us?” Luke asked.
“Your uncle came looking for me.”
Luke moved nearer Daniel, keeping Laura in sight.
“The same energy, the same people,” Luke said to Daniel. “She could lead them straight here.”
“She stays,” Daniel said.
Luke looked at her. She did not apologize. Daniel had not asked her to.
The ceramic connector lay on the cabinet where Luke had left it.
Daniel walked past him without looking at it.
The new machine stood on a trolley beneath a work lamp.
Three copper coils encircled a glass cylinder. At one end, a brass funnel opened toward the room. Two round meters sat in a small control box on the shelf below.
Laura moved closer.
The glass was empty. A thick cable hung down beside one wheel, its loose end resting on the floor.
Daniel lifted it and draped it over the trolley rail before she could step on it.
“One connection to finish,” Daniel said.
Luke told him about the connector. His uncle glanced toward the cabinet. “Good.”
Laura ran a gloved finger along the trolley's edge. The cylinder was wider than her forearm and about as long as the space between her hands when she held them apart.
Daniel traced the coils with one finger. “The intake gathers the energy. These direct it into the collector. Once he's within reach, he won't have the freedom he's accustomed to.”
“Show me.”
Daniel raised the loose cable. “Not until this is finished. The principle worked in my earlier collector.”
“The one the police took,” Luke said.
Daniel ignored him.
blocks.alt: Daniel presents an empty glass-cylinder collector with three copper coils on a trolley to Laura while Luke watches skeptically.

blocks.text: The loose cable looked less convincing than his explanation.
Laura took her hand off the trolley.
“What do you need me for?” Laura asked.
“He knows you. You can ask him to meet you.”
She studied the brass funnel. “He stays near the lake. He won't walk into your laboratory.”
“Then we won't use it here.” Daniel nudged the trolley. It rolled a few inches before the cable caught against a wheel.
“When it's ready,” she said. “And you'll have to show me where.”
“We'll choose somewhere suitable.”
She looked at him. He had made the plan sound as though part of it belonged to her.
Luke drifted nearer the trolley.
“And when do you work on my body?” Luke asked.
Laura looked at Luke again, this time more carefully. The iron plates hid so much of his face that she had not noticed the tightness around his eyes.
“We've discussed this,” Daniel said.
“Before we had a laboratory. Before we had equipment. We've got both now.”
“And I intend to use them. This is an opportunity we can't allow to pass.”
“So she comes first.”
Daniel finally faced him.
“For once, could you think beyond your own immediate concerns?”
Luke backed away from the trolley.
Laura could have looked elsewhere while they argued. She watched.
Daniel waited until Luke had moved to the far bench.
“You'll have to excuse him.”
Luke could still hear every word.
Laura looked at the cylinder.
“If I bring him there, I want to be there when you use it,” Laura said. “I want him to know I chose it.”
Daniel nodded. “Of course.”
She imagined the little face looking from the machine to her. No more lessons. No patient explanations of what she ought to try next.
“All right,” she said. “I'll help you.”
Luke turned from the other bench.
“Well, welcome, Lava Lips.”
He put enough weight on the name to make her look at him.
“You sound frightened.”
“Of you?”
“You're the one who keeps asking whether I brought somebody.”
Daniel raised a hand.
“Enough. Luke, bring me the connector.”
Luke looked at the cabinet, then at his uncle.
“Get it yourself.”
Daniel's hand stayed in the air for a moment. Then he lowered it and turned back to Laura.
“Come tomorrow. I'll have more to show you.”
She gave the cylinder one last look.
“I'll expect it.”
Laura went home by the lake.
At the slipway, the old earth bank was dark in the evening light. She paused above the concrete slope, thinking of the polished copper coils beneath Daniel's lamp.
A small glow moved beyond the rocks.
She might have kept walking. Instead, she waited.
Flaming Head stopped near the edge of the water.
“I've found someone to work with,” Laura said. “Daniel Orkleson.”
Flaming Head stopped moving. She noticed immediately.
“Laura, he's hurt people.”
“So have I.”
“You didn't mean to.”
She looked toward the rocks. “You don't know what I mean to do.”
blocks.alt: Laura in costume refuses a troubled Flaming Head’s warning at the familiar lakeside practice place.

blocks.text: “What has he asked you for?”
“That's between us.”
“I know what his equipment did to someone else.”
She thought of Luke above the cabinet. The jaw. The empty space beneath it.
“He says you've interfered with his work.”
“I was trying to stop him hurting someone.”
Laura stepped away from the slope. “Then you won't like what we're doing.”
He moved as though to follow, then stopped over the rocks.
She had not told him where the workshop was. She had not told him about the cylinder or the funnel or the part he would play.
She liked knowing something he did not.
“I'll be seeing you,” she said.
She left him by the water.
Back at the workshop, Daniel had fetched the connector himself. Luke watched from above the empty stool while his uncle tightened a screw inside the control box.
“You really trust her?”
“I trust that she's angry.”
“She told you he gave her the suit.”
“And she told us what she thinks of him.” Daniel tested the fitting with one finger. “We can use that.”
Luke drifted nearer. “You let her call me that.”
Daniel looked up. “Call you what?”
Luke stared at him until recognition crossed his face.
“It was an unfortunate introduction,” Daniel said. “We need her cooperation.”
“You weren't the one she was looking at.”
His uncle reached for the lid. “I have work to do.”
The Army ray lay unused on the bench beside Luke. Across the room, Daniel fitted the control box beneath the empty cylinder.
Luke watched the two meter needles. Neither had moved all evening.
blocks.alt: Luke hovers apart beside the untouched Army ray while Daniel works on the unfinished collector, Laura absent.

blocks.text: He stayed to watch them anyway.
